questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding the cervix except:

options.label: C
options.text: Position of the squamocolumnar junction is fixed

options.label: D
options.text: Transformation zone is susceptible to HPV infection

questions.answerText: Position of the squamocolumnar junction is fixed
questions.solutionHtml:
Position of the squamocolumnar junction is fixed
  • The position of the squamocolumnar junction (the boundary between the squamous epithelium of the ectocervix and the columnar epithelium of the endocervix) is not fixed.
  • It can vary in position and can move over time, especially in response to hormonal changes or with certain conditions such as pregnancy or inflammation.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1001

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding cervical infection by HPV infection except

options.label: B
options.text: High-risk HPVs are also implicated in SCC arising at many other sites

options.label: C
options.text: It preferentially Infects mature squamous epithelial cells

options.label: D
options.text: The cancer-producing capability is because of E6 and E7 protein

questions.answerText: It preferentially Infects mature squamous epithelial cells
questions.solutionHtml:
It preferentially Infects mature squamous epithelial cells
  • HPV infection primarily affects basal cells of the squamous epithelium, not mature squamous cells.
  • The virus enters the basal cells and disrupts their normal growth and differentiation, leading to abnormal cell changes and potential progression to cancer.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1002

questions.stem: What is the most common HPV stereotype associated with Adenocarcinoma of the cervix?
questions.solutionHtml:
18
  • HPV-18 is known to be strongly associated with the development of cervical adenocarcinoma.
  • It is one of the high-risk HPV genotypes that can lead to the progression of cervical lesions to invasive adenocarcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1003

questions.stem: What are the features of pilocytic change caused by HPV?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • Nuclear enlargement, Nuclear hyperchromasia, and Perinuclear halo are all features of Koilocytic changes caused by HPV. Hence, the correct answer is D. All of the above


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1003

questions.stem: At the ultrastructural level, the perinuclear halo shows the cytoplasmic effect of which viral protein?
questions.solutionHtml:
E5
  • The perinuclear halo observed at the ultrastructural level in infected cells is associated with the cytoplasmic effect of the E5 viral protein of HPV (Human Papillomavirus).


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1003

questions.stem: Which of the following would not be seen in a colonoscopies biopsy of a patient with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Breach in basement membrane
  • A breach in the basement membrane is not typically observed in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). CIN represents abnormal cellular changes within the cervical epithelium.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1003

questions.stemHtml: Based on the characteristic cytological findings on PAP smear examination in a 26-year-old female presented for screening. What’s your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
LSIL
  • The given image of PAP cytology shows a low nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, nuclear irregularity, hyperchromasia, perinuclear halo, and binucleation which are suggestible of cellular changes seen in low-grade lesions.
  • LSIL represents mild dysplastic changes in the squamous epithelial cells, indicating a lower risk for the development of invasive squamous cell carcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1003

questions.stemHtml: Based on the histological features of a cervical biopsy showing tumor infiltration into the stroma, the diagram is shown below, Identify the type of tumor:
questions.solutionHtml:
Squamous cell carcinoma
  • The histopathological image showing nests and tongues of malignant squamous epithelium infiltrating the stroma is suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma.
  • It is the most common type of cervical cancer and is characterized by the presence of malignant squamous epithelial cells invading the surrounding stromal tissue.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th Edition, Page No. 1005
